# Review — ani-017-e

## Pass 1

Checks run by script: the glyph sequence of units.json equals the packet's exactly (125 packet words, 443 signs, same codes in the same order); rubric flags match the packet word by word (41 rubric words in the units = the packet's 40, with Budge's rubric group erṭāit-nef split into rdyt + n·f); the one restored sign (D37 in rdyt) is flagged and no other; every word's morph covers all its glyphs; every `q` has one index per glyph and the splits/joins (in + n·f, rdyt + n·f, m-sꜣ, pḥ·n) are re-indexed correctly. Names and `say` agree with the published parts (Khepri, Ra, Isis, Nephthys, Anubis, Osiris, Shu, Atum, Horus, Seth, Ruti, Neni-nesu, Ani); pw tr rf sw, ky ḏd, wꜥbt, swꜣ, m-sꜣ, iṯ (V13 + D54), rwti, ṯs-pẖr follow the published spellings and renderings.

### Changes
- U0 · l · minor · "were-brought" for a singular subject (msyt) and against i "was brought" · changed to "was-brought".
- U0 · n · minor · msyt "evening meal" and ṯḥnt "faience" were presented as "taken as" without saying the sense is doubtful · added a sentence: both are the best the signs give but not sure; a meal "of faience" is strange, Budge takes ṯḥnt for a plant; the bead-collar sign (if rightly read) and the mineral grains are why faience is preferred.
- U4 · l, i · minor · ḥsw "filth" given as certain in l/i though Aa2 is approximate (one reader F52) and the reading of the word is a guess · "filth(?)" in l and i.
- U4 · n · minor · same: added "the reading is not sure" after the ḥs identification.
- U4 · n · minor · grg said to be written "as in the Spell 125 address"; the address writes grg g-r with T14, no U17; the U17 spelling with g and r as complements is the published weighing of the heart · reference changed to "the weighing of the heart".
- U10 · n · minor · the stray Q1 (Budge's "(sic)") was left unread, i.e. treated as a doubled sign, but the note did not use the misprint formula and mixed this with alternatives it says do not fit · note now opens "The papyrus writes the seat twice, st wsir; read wsir."; the alternatives (st "seat", ꜣst) are kept as considered and set aside. Glyphs unchanged (Q1 stays, role phon, empty tr, as published unread signs such as Z9 in rf).
- U11 · morph · minor · lemma "snt" for "found, lay out (a building)": the lemma is snṯ; the signs write t · lemma changed to snṯ, reading left snt (what the signs write).
- U11 · n · minor · same: note now says snṯ written with t for ṯ (as with iṯ·n·f, l. 131).
- U11 · n · minor · agentless passive "built (by) Atum" not clearly marked doubtful · added "so the reading is not sure" after the supplied in "by".
- U11 · i · style · "the Double Lion" against the published rendering "Double-Lion" (Spell 125 declarations) · changed to "the Double-Lion".
- U12 · l, i, n · major · twri ḥr nṯrty stẖ read as two active transitive verbs, "Horus purifies, Seth makes divine", with no object written, and nṯrty glossed "make divine" from nṯri, which is "be divine" (the causative would be s-nṯr); the note also called nṯrty "in the same form as twri" though it has an ending ty that twri lacks · re-read as two sentences of quality, verb before noun: "pure is Horus, divine(?) is Seth", twr "be clean, pure" (as the address takes twri, a state) and nṯri "be divine"; endings i / ty said to be unexplained; the active reading is mentioned and why it is weaker; the closing sentence now ties the sense to ṯs-pẖr. l: "has-arrived · the-remedy(?) · pure · Horus · divine(?) · Seth · and-vice-versa"; i: "The remedy(?) has arrived: Horus is pure and Seth is divine(?), and the other way round."

### Refused / checked and left
- U0 in n·f as passive sḏm "was brought": the alternative in·n·f (sḏm·n·f) is stated; the passive is supported by the gloss's rdyt n·f. Left.
- U0 tꜣnnt: X1 before U30 as `comp` t, M22 M22 as n n with N35 N35 complements — matches published nn (M22 M22 N35 N35). Left.
- U1 tr with M17 `phon i` not in the reading: same as published ani-017-a/c. Left.
- U3 bntt "baboons(?)" — marked "(?)" and "The reading is uncertain"; Budge agrees on the sense (apes); the feminine-dual idea is offered as a possibility only. Left.
- U3 ꜣst Q1 `log ꜣs`: matches published. Left.
- U5 ꜥfdt with t written before d: graphic grouping (X1 over D46), not a slip; the note says so. No misprint formula. Left.
- U5 mꜥẖtw "innards(?)": marked doubtful in l, i and n; F32 and F51 approximate. Left.
- U5 ẖr (T28) as "holding": new lemma ẖr kept distinct from ḫr "before" (the weighing of the heart files T28 under ḫr; that is the published part's matter, not this draft's).
- U6 rdyt "was given": a vague label, but the note says the ending yt is unexplained and gives the participle alternative; the quoted-clause reading after ir fits the answer wsir pw. Left.
- U8 qnqn "beating(?)" with nt that does not agree: marked doubtful, alternative ("the Beater of the Two Lands") given, the difficulty of nt stated. Left.
- U8 nni-nsw with X1 `phon t` not read: matches published (ani-017-a: "the t is part of the writing of nsw and not read"). Left.
- U10 smꜣt "place of union(?)": marked doubtful, burial sense mentioned as possible. New lemma smꜣt (the known smꜣ is "kill"). Left.
- U11 rwti: E23 phon / E23 comp as in ani-spell125-opening; V13 for t explained. Left.
- U12 rrt "remedy(?)": marked doubtful; Budge "drugs" agrees on sense. Left.
- U13 iṯ·n·f with V13 `phon iṯ` + D54 `det` and X1 as complement: as published ani-017-b (iṯt). Left.
- U14 ntf tm "He is Atum": plain nominal sentence; the wording is forced by the grammar, not taken from Budge. Left.
- No Budge-isms in any l / i ("triumphant" in Budge's mꜣꜥ-ḫrw rendered "true of voice"; no "saith", "homage").
